'''Millard Henry Alexander''' (born February 17, 1943, Boston, Massachusetts) is an American theoretical chemist. He is Distinguished University Professor<ref name=umd_dup>{{cite web |url=https://faculty.umd.edu/awards/list_dup.html |title=List of Distinguished University Professors, University of Maryland}}</ref> at the [[University of Maryland]], with appointments in the Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry<ref name=umd>{{cite web |url=http://www.chem.umd.edu/millard-alexander/ |title=University of Maryland, Chemistry Faculty Profile for Millard Henry Alexander}}</ref> and the Institute for Physical Science and Technology.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ipst.umd.edu/researchandfaculty/mha.php |title=Institute for Physical Science and Technology, University of Maryland, College Park}}</ref> He is the author of over 300 publications and an active researcher in the fields of molecular collision dynamics and theoretical chemistry.

==Research==
Alexander's research focus is the quantum-mechanical aspects of molecular collisions, in particular those involving [[open shell|open-shell]] species. More specifically, Alexander's work has focused on understanding chemical reactions where the [[Born–Oppenheimer approximation]] can be violated, by means of [[nonadiabatic coupling]], [[spin–orbit interaction]]s and [[conical intersection]]s.<ref name=iaqms/> Alexander's work is particularly important in understanding the {{nobr|F + H<sub>2</sub> → FH + H}} and {{nobr|Cl + H<sub>2</sub> → HCl + H}} reactions.<ref name=althorpe>{{citation |title=Quantum scattering calculations on chemical reactions |first1=S. C. |last1=Althorpe |first2=D. C. |last2=Clary |journal=Annu. Rev. Phys. Chem. |volume=54 |year=2003 |pages=493–529 |doi=10.1146/annurev.physchem.54.011002.103750 |pmid=12651964 |issn=0066-426X |bibcode=2003ARPC...54..493A }}.</ref><ref name=liu>{{citation |title=Recent advances in crossed-beam studies of bimolecular reactions |first1=K. P. |last1=Liu |journal=J. Chem. Phys. |volume=125 |page=132307 |year=2006 |doi=10.1063/1.2216706 |pmid=17029426 |issn=0021-9606 |issue=13 |bibcode=2006JChPh.125m2307L }}.</ref>

==Organisational affiliations==
Alexander is a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] and of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] and a  member of the [[International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science]]. In 2015 he received the Herschbach Medal for contributions to the theoretical study of the dynamics of molecular collisions.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.chem.wayne.edu/dmc2015/prize.html |title=Dynamics of Molecular Collisions, Herschbach Medal, 2015|date=15 November 2023 }}</ref>

Since 2012 Alexander has served as the President of the [http://www.telluridescience.org Telluride Science Research Center].<ref name=TSRC>{{cite web |url=http://telluridescience.org/about/governance |title=Telluride Science Research Center, Board of Directors}}</ref>
